newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish lawmakers back country's allotment holders.
newsitem.headline: Polish lawmakers back country's allotment holders.

text.p: Poland's lawmakers on Friday backed almost one million Poles who want to keep their beloved allotment gardens even though many are on prime urban land needed for roads and schools.
Parliament voted by 267 votes to 74 with eight abstentions to uphold a new law handing huge tracts of valuable urban real estate on a 99-year lease to the Polish Association of Allotment Holders.
Such gardens with their little summer houses give millions of Poles a weekend escape from cramped apartments and enable them to grow food or flowers for sale to flesh out meagre incomes.
The ruling affects 44,000 hectares of land around the country, much of it prime urban building land estimated to be worth between $1 billion and $2 billion in Warsaw alone.
City councils who lease the allotments out had complained that some of the land was needed for vital housing, roads and other developments.
In November the Constitutional Tribunal upheld the objections and rejected the decision to grant control to one association of allotment holders.
Poland's ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance and its Peasant party allies who backed the law said they were safeguarding plot holders.
Poland faces parliamentary elections this year and some chiefs of the allotment holders' association have promised to back the SLD in return for its support.
